Hi Ben / EdgeFin team,

Thanks again for the call earlier — good to align on scope. Quick recap and next steps so we can get the benchmark scheduled:  

Recap from today's discovery:
- Business goal: validate that the Redwood hosted serving path meets your latency SLOs for the new risk-scoring endpoint and to quantify unit cost at target throughput.
- SLO targets you mentioned: p95 latency goal ~200ms for completed responses; streaming token-level updates required for the UI.
- Scale: expected steady-state concurrency ~50 concurrent sessions, peak burst to ~200 concurrent sessions; steady throughput target roughly 200 requests/sec during peak scenarios.
- Model/inputs: proprietary risk-scoring model (EdgeFin-run), prompt lengths generally 80–250 tokens, average output ~120 tokens.

Agreed next steps:
1) You to share a representative prompt set and a small sample of sensitive/PII-masked records (we'll treat any raw data as confidential).
2) We will share our benchmark harness and measurement definitions (attached: rdw_benchmark_harness_instructions.md, benchmark_results_template.xlsx).
3) Tentative benchmark window: week of Nov 9 — please confirm availability for Nov 10–11 for an initial run.
4) Technical clarifications from our side (Dev will follow up with measurement details on warm-up, cache behavior, and reproducibility).

Attachments: edgefin_prompt_set_v1.jsonl (sample prompts), benchmark_results_template.xlsx (results template), rdw_benchmark_harness_instructions.md (harness overview).

If the targets above look right, confirm and Ben can drop the full prompt set (or a link) and we’ll schedule the run.

Marissa,

Thanks for the clear recap — that matches what we discussed. A few clarifications from our end:  
- Target: we'd like p95 end-to-end latency <= 200ms for the full completed response where possible. For streaming, we need token-level flushes within 30–50ms of generation (the UI renders partial updates).
- Concurrency: 50 sustained, with 200 concurrent users as brief peaks (1–3 minutes).
- Throughput: 200 req/s peak, sustained 80–120 req/s outside of peak windows.

Attached is a slightly expanded prompt set (redacted) — see edgefin_prompt_set_v1.jsonl. Alice (cc'd) will be our technical lead for the run and will coordinate any environment access or sample payloads.

We can make Nov 10 available for an initial run in the morning (ET). Please confirm UTC windows and any required whitelisting of IPs if you're calling our internal endpoints.

Subject: Re: Performance SLO benchmark methodology exchange

Hi Ben — quick technical follow-up on measurement methodology so we get apples-to-apples results:  

Measurement definitions we propose:
- Warm-up: 30 minutes of load with gradually increasing concurrency to populate KV cache and JITs. Warm-up samples excluded from reported metrics.
- Sample size: at least 10k requests across the prompt set for the core report; we can run smaller quick-pass (2k) runs for early validation.
- Latency metrics: report p50, p90, p95, p99 for both total request latency and per-token latency (for streaming). Also include mean and tail plots.
- Throughput metrics: sustained requests/sec and tokens/sec; report variance over 1-minute windows.
- Concurrency: measure measured latency curves at 10/25/50/100/200 concurrent sessions.
- Streaming behavior: measure time-to-first-token and token inter-arrival distribution; for streaming, we’ll instrument with an event-side tracer to capture token flush times.
- Reproducibility: we will capture harness version, model commit hash, quantization profile, and seed configuration. We recommend using deterministic seeds for generation where possible; note that some tokenizers/models have non-deterministic kernels — we'll flag those.
- Environmental controls: fixed instance types, same network egress path, and disabled background jobs during runs.

Questions for you:
1) Do you require the benchmark to run against your internal endpoint (EdgeFin-hosted model) or our Redwood-hosted replica? If EdgeFin-hosted, we’ll need a short-lived test user + IP allowlist.
2) Are there any non-deterministic transformation steps in your prompt pipeline (e.g., async lookup calls) we should be aware of?
3) Any compliance constraints around telemetry/trace collection? We can redact payloads and only capture timing metadata.

I'll drop a short harness README in the shared Drive and a minimal script to run the quick-pass so you can validate locally before the full run.

Thanks,
Dev Patel
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference
dev.patel@redwoodinference.com
